title: 7.3 · Playtest party
name: Playtest party
summary: Teams of three hand in first, then three rotations: hosts and players swap, and each player fills a Playtest Tally (fun 1 to 5, too easy to too hard, where I got stuck on a storyboard panel, one wish). Makers enter the tallies in My Data, read the bar chart, write the claim and send the one fix the data supports; the class pools every team's counts on the board.
iCan: collect feedback from many players with a tally sheet
use the numbers to refine one rule and explain the change
say what pooling the whole class's tallies shows that one team's cards cannot
materials: Playtest Tally printable (fun 1 to 5; too easy, about right, too hard; I got stuck at; one wish; four per tester)
the playtest protocol printable (one per team) and the role cards: Player, Watcher, Note-taker
the team folders with the captains' login cards
the class tally drawn on the board: fun, too hard, most common wish
doNow: What is the hardest part of watching someone play your game? Then: how many testers would it take before you trust what they say?
plan: Arrive, captains log in and hand in, Do Now
Explore: the protocol, the tally sheet and one row in My Data
Playtest: two rotations of 5 minutes, then tally, claim and one fix (8)

warmup.why: two retrieval items from build day (which had no warm-up of its own), one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from build day

do: Put the protocol on the projector: hand in first; three rotations; Player, Watcher (the maker, silent) and Note-taker; be specific, be kind, say what not who, never write a name.

Hold up the Playtest Tally: fun 1 to 5; too easy, about right, too hard; I got stuck at, tapped on a storyboard panel; one wish. Fill one for the frog quiz with the class and enter it as the first row of a My Data tally in Data Detective on the projector.
say: One tester is a story; nine testers are data. Tally the sheets, chart them, and let the bar tell you which one thing to change.
A change the data supports sounds like this: seven of nine found level 2 too hard, so level 2 gets easier, then we test again. Not: add a level 3.
ask: Seven of nine testers rated level 2 too hard. What change does the data support, and what change does it not?
explore.afterAsk: An easier level 2, then test again; not a harder level 1, not a new level 3, not a new title. Write the claim frame on the board: ___ of ___ testers ___, so we ___.
explore.bigIdea: Many testers make data; the data picks the one change.

play.protocol: peer playtest, three rotations, the tally in My Data
play.handIn: captains hand in at the start of the period: a clean scan is visible to the class at once; a flagged build waits for a human and is played from the maker's screen
rotations: Rotation 1 (5 minutes): half the teams host; the other half play two games each and fill a Playtest Tally for each.
Rotation 2 (5 minutes): swap hosts and players.

Rotation 3 (8 minutes): makers enter their tallies as a My Data tally in Data Detective (one row per tester), read the bar chart, write the claim (seven of nine found level 2 too hard), send the one fix message the data supports, play it, and hand in again. One teammate adds the team's counts to the class tally on the board.
play.myData: Data Detective, chapter My Data (Pro), tally mode; if the game asks for a quest code, it is 7 2 2 0. The tally stays on the maker's device; nothing crosses players
play.pooled: the class tally on the board (how many games were rated too hard, the average fun, the most common wish) is the crowdsourced view no single team's sheets give
play.roles: Player · Watcher (the maker: silent, notes where the player gets stuck) · Note-taker; the roles rotate, so everyone watches once
play.rules: be specific, be kind, say what not who, never write a name; the maker says thank you only
lookFors: a fix the tally does not support (a new feature, a new title): point at the bar
a tally with one row: send them to play one more game before rotation 3 ends
a Watcher explaining the game to the tester
play.misconception: Students think more testers just means more opinions; the point is that many tallies become a sample you can count, and the count, not the loudest tester, picks the change.
earlyFinishers: play a third game and add a row to that team's tally
read the class tally on the board and write one claim about the whole class's games

discuss: What did players do that you never expected?
What does the class tally show that no single team's sheets could?
showMe: One team shows its My Data bar chart on the projector, reads the claim, and names the one fix message it sent.

States a claim with the count (how many of how many) and the change it supports

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: What is the hardest part of watching someone play your game? Then: how many testers would it take before you trust what they say?

Big idea: Many testers make data; the data picks the one change.

Today: hand in first, then three rotations. Host, play, then tally, claim and fix one thing.

We will talk about:
- What did players do that you never expected?
- What does the class tally show that no single team's sheets could?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Playtest protocol
steps.body:
Hand in your game first.

Two rotations, then the tally:
- Rotation 1: half the teams host, half play. Play two games. Fill one Playtest Tally for each: fun 1 to 5; too easy, about right or too hard; I got stuck at (tap the storyboard panel); one wish.
- Rotation 2: swap.
- Then: makers enter the tallies in My Data, read the bar, write the claim, send one fix message, play it, hand in again. One teammate adds your counts to the class tally on the board.

Roles: Player · Watcher (the maker: silent, note where the player gets stuck) · Note-taker.

Rules: be specific, be kind, say what not who, never write a name. The maker says thank you, and nothing else.

steps.title: Tally and the one change

levels: Attempted: fewer than four sheets, or sheets with no tally
Meets: four or more sheets tallied and charted, one change the tally supports made and explained, the team's counts in the class tally
Exceeds: a second round of ratings recorded after the change

steps.body:
Write your tally:
- How many sheets did you get?
- Fun: how many of each score from 1 to 5? Too easy, about right, too hard: how many of each?
- Which panel did players get stuck at most? Which wish came up most?
- Your claim: ___ of ___ testers ___.
- The one change the data supports, and the fix message you sent.
- What happened when you played it after the fix?
- What did the class tally on the board show that your own sheets did not?

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about feedback, tallies and the changes they support.

steps.title: In your own words
steps.body:
Write your claim from the tally, the one change the data supports, and what the pooled class tally added.
Frame: ___ of ___ testers said ___, so we changed ___. The class tally showed ___.
